items.title: I made a Love, Death & Robots-inspired screensaver to see what my AI agent is doing
items.content: I've been working on TOTS (Thoughts On Terminal Screen), a small open-source screensaver for Hermes Agent. I have an old laptop for my Hermes Agent that stays on my desk, and I wanted a way to see what my agent was doing without constantly checking the terminal or Telegram. TOTS listens to the agent's reasoning, responses, and tool activity, turning them into scrolling pixelated emojis. The animation is inspired by the title sequences of Love, Death & Robots. The idea is pretty simple: while the agent is working, the display keeps moving. When it becomes idle, the animation gradually settles down. It's meant to be something you can notice in your peripheral vision without demanding your attention. It started as an experiment inspired by GERTY from Moon, but I eventually moved away from facial expressions and ended up with this terminal-based approach. It supports custom themes, multiple sessions and subagents, and a debug mode that shows in real time what's going on in the background. Under the hood, a small plugin streams events through a local socket. Short phrases are matched against a customizable CSV to select emojis. You can also provide your own Python converter if you want something more sophisticated.  No extra AI inference needed.  Offline/Local friendly & Open source. GitHub: https://github.com/anderson-/TOTS I'd be interested to hear what you think, especially about the visual approach.    submitted by    /u/_apekind_    to    r/hermesagent   [link]   [comments]
